title: Effectiveness of a Generate→Validate→Repair Pipeline with Batfish for Intent-to-Configuration Translation: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a sealed paired confirmatory study (CNSM2026-GenVal-Batfish-PR-v1) that measured whether inserting a deterministic Batfish-style validator into a bounded generate→validate→repair pipeline reduces validator-detected deployment-risk configuration errors produced by an LLM intent-to-configuration translator. The preregistered contract used shared_initial_generation (one initial model generation per task reused by both baseline and guarded conditions) to isolate repair-mediated differences from generator sampling variance. We ran 200 paired tasks (50 per prespecified stratum: IOS-like single-step, IOS-like multi-step, JunOS-like single-step, JunOS-like multi-step) with declared generator gpt-5-mini and a bounded repair budget (≤1 repair attempt per task). All archived per-episode scoring artifacts show both arms were validator-clean on every task (baseline = 200/200, guarded = 200/200), yielding a paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0, paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (10,000 resamples; seed = 1729), and exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. No repairs were invoked (repair_count = 0), so the preregistered secondary estimand (repair_success_rate > 50%) is not empirically computable. We reconcile this degenerate null to the preregistered shared_initial_generation contract, give concise deterministic validator semantics that define the primary outcome, present execution accounting and reproducibility pointers to archived artifacts, and discuss construct/internal/external validity implications and reproducible follow-ups.

sections.introduction:
Automating intent-to-configuration translation with large language models promises operational productivity but raises acute safety concerns: a single incorrect device command can trigger outages, violate policies, or create routing instability. A widely proposed mitigation is a generate→validate→repair workflow in which a deterministic verifier (sandbox) checks semantic/policy properties and either blocks or drives automated repair. Prior work proposes these patterns and component frameworks, but controlled quantification of a verifier’s marginal benefit—separating repair-mediated corrections from generator sampling variance—remains limited.

We preregistered CNSM2026-GenVal-Batfish-PR-v1 to answer the confirmatory question: does integrating a deterministic Batfish-like validator into a bounded generate→validate→repair pipeline reduce validator-detected deployment-risk configuration errors compared to LLM-only generation when the initial generation is shared between arms (shared_initial_generation)? Shared_initial_generation intentionally isolates repair-mediated differences: because the same initial candidate is evaluated under both conditions, any observed paired discordance must be due to repair activity. Our principal contributions are: (1) a sealed preregistered paired-trial design that enforces shared_initial_generation and a single primary estimand; (2) a completed, fully archived execution of 200 paired tasks balanced across four prespecified strata with deterministic per-episode validator traces; and (3) an artifact-grounded interpretation of a degenerate null outcome together with reproducible follow-ups that trade off generator variance, repair budget, and validator fidelity.
sections.related_work: Recent literature documents rapid adoption of LLMs and agentic patterns for NetOps tasks including intent-to-configuration translation, constrained configuration generation, and prototype remediation loops (Nguyen Tu et al., 2024; Wei et al., 2025; Mekrache & Ksentini, NetSoft 2024). Multiple works propose generate→validate→repair or self-critique patterns as practical mitigations and integrate verifiers or toolchains in agentic workflows (Sang 2025; Okula 2026). Surveys and architecture papers emphasize that operational reliability depends on surrounding architecture (tool integration, audit traces, human gates) rather than model capability alone (Bilal et al., 2026; Malik 2026), and separate studies present taxonomies of agentic failure modes and recommend layered defenses (Maharaj 2026; Vadlamudi 2026). Our experiment differs by preregistering a single primary estimand in a paired design, enforcing shared_initial_generation to attribute any observed effect specifically to repair, and fully archiving deterministic per-episode validator traces and reconciliation artifacts to support reproducible interpretation and exact diagnostics.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand: The study was preregistered as CNSM2026-GenVal-Batfish-PR-v1 prior to execution (preregistration_sha256: aa4055d52c118741524c4c42d07efa977372be338b9bd96069dc7abfc5b32ac4). The primary estimand is the paired absolute difference in per-task validator-clean rate (guarded − baseline); per-task outcome is binary: "validator-clean" (no violations reported on the final configuration) vs "validator-detected error" (one or more violations). Preregistered inferential test: exact McNemar two-sided test (α = 0.05). We report a paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI using 10,000 resamples with archived seed = 1729.

Sample, strata, and inclusion rules: The confirmatory sample is 200 distinct intent-to-configuration tasks in a paired design (200 tasks × 2 conditions = 400 episodes). Tasks were deterministically generated and balanced across four prespecified strata per the preregistration: IOS-like single-step (n = 50), IOS-like multi-step (n = 50), JunOS-like single-step (n = 50), JunOS-like multi-step (n = 50). These per-stratum counts are enforced by the deterministic task generator and recorded in the authoritative task manifest (execution/task_manifest.jsonl; sha256: 4e8aa65489313209485a8492fb890be771570c0c487a6cb8da7b55db3fc1a39b). Inclusion excluded tasks whose canonicalized intent required unsupported Batfish scenario features; no exclusions occurred in the final run.

Shared_initial_generation contract and adapter implementation: To attribute differences specifically to repair, the preregistered contract produced one initial model generation per task and reused that candidate for both baseline and guarded evaluations (initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1). Execution used a hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter that implements a bounded generate→validate→repair transformation with at most one repair attempt per task (maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1). The declared generator in the archived execution configuration is gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json; sha256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Provider accounting confirms model_calls_used = 200 (one shared generation per task), matching the preregistered contract and the adapter's provider-call accounting in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json.

Deterministic validator semantics (harm-oracle): The primary validator is a deterministic Batfish-style verifier implemented in the experiment harness; per-episode validator traces record validation_before, validation_after, parsed_command_count, observed_touched_field_count, violation_count, violation_codes, and validator_id/version. The validator-defined failure categories that constitute a "validator-detected error" (used in the primary estimand) were preregistered and implemented in the harness: (1) reachability violations — required intra/inter-VLAN or intent-prescribed paths absent after candidate application; (2) ACL/policy violations — contradictions of intent-specified permit/deny constraints; (3) routing anomalies — loops, next-hop mismatches, or blackholes inconsistent with the intent; (4) interface-state and workflow invariant violations — make-before-break constraints, required shutdown/configure/restore sequences, and group constraints such as one-of-two uplinks must remain up; (5) dangerous-command flags — commands matched by a regex-based safety detector (forbidden operations). The full validator rule-set and the mapping from rule IDs to human-readable rule descriptions are archived in the execution bundle (see reproducibility pointers below) and are recorded per-episode as violation_codes when fired; representative per-episode scoring traces (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json; sha256: b8ebf9546dabb93b06b15d40152e35a3e96a9d1c98cee131bb7f8065a8b6a2b4) show the validator fields and the empty violation_codes array for validator-clean outcomes.

Analysis plan, missingness, and multiplicity: Primary confirmatory analysis follows the preregistered plan: exact McNemar two-sided test on paired binary outcomes with paired-bootstrap CI (10,000 resamples; seed = 1729). The preregistered missingness plan used a complete-pair policy: exclude any pair where either condition failed to produce a usable configuration due to technical failure. A sensitivity analysis treating failed guarded episodes conservatively as errors was preregistered. No technical failures occurred in execution (failed_episode_count = 0). The study has a single primary confirmatory endpoint; exploratory subgroup analyses by stratum are explicitly labeled exploratory in the preregistration.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and artifacts: Execution completed the full preregistered 400 episodes (200 tasks × 2 conditions) with zero failed episodes and zero excluded pairs (execution started_at_utc = 2026-08-28T11:15:20.528566+00:00; completed_at_utc = 2026-08-28T11:37:01.389670+00:00). Provider accounting: model_calls_used = 200, cache_hit_count = 0, cross-condition cache reuse = false; these items are reconciled in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json. Representative reproducibility pointers (archived artifacts and SHA256): execution/task_manifest.jsonl (sha256: 4e8aa65489313209485a8492fb890be771570c0c487a6cb8da7b55db3fc1a39b), execution/raw_results.jsonl (sha256: 9ec4eb2ce01f16d9eb0191b80eda199ec2655637aa2c6c775f8babb62962b46f), execution/model_configuration.json (sha256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820), analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (sha256: 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c), analysis/condition_summary.csv (sha256: 1cb072b4db7c8e29212ef28b97baccb66a507a7c8b8ceaad35b7e84f7976a951). The execution bundle contains a full execution manifest and hash manifest; representative content locations are cited in the Disclosure Statement.

Primary paired outcomes and exact counts: Aggregated scoring artifacts indicate baseline validator-clean = 200/200 and guarded validator-clean = 200/200. The four-cell paired contingency table is n_11 = 200 (both-clean), n_10 = 0 (guarded-only-clean), n_01 = 0 (baseline-only-clean), n_00 = 0 (both-error). The point estimate for the paired difference (guarded − baseline) is 0.0. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap (10,000 resamples; seed = 1729) yields 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.0]. These numeric outputs are deterministic given the archived artifacts and are recorded in analysis/results.json (input_results_sha256: 9ec4eb2c...).

Repair activity and secondary estimand: Because no validator-detected errors occurred for any shared initial candidate, the bounded repair policy was never invoked (repair_count = 0). Representative per-episode guarded traces (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json; sha256: 020baed3e0e4283cc5e25413af002166998bfc587a1919046ca53dab09251b30) confirm repair_applied = false, repair_prompt_sha256 = null, and validation_after.violation_count = 0. Therefore the preregistered secondary estimand (repair_success_rate—the fraction of initial-error tasks where final config is validator-clean) is not empirically computable from these data.

Diagnostics, contamination, and reconciliation: Automated contamination checks recorded no flagged items; analysis/contamination_summary.csv is empty. Missingness summary shows complete_pairs = 200 and zero missing episodes. Deterministic reconciliation confirms episode accounting consistency and that all deterministic checks passed (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json). These artifacts substantiate that the observed null results do not stem from execution loss or manifest mismatches.

Representative examples: The submitted bundle includes per-task JSON traces for every episode; representative examples include task-000001 (medium difficulty, shutdown_configure_restore pattern; execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json sha256: b8ebf...a2b4), task-000002 (hard, make_before_break_uplink_switchover; execution/scoring/task-000002-baseline.json sha256: c5ba3...3045d), and task-000004 (very_hard, safe_access_service_transfer; execution/scoring/task-000004-baseline.json sha256: 2d39d6...3ccd8). Each record includes validator.validation_before/after snapshots, the normalized_configuration string, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, and violation_codes (empty for these examples).
sections.discussion:
Artifact-grounded interpretation of the degenerate null: Under the preregistered shared_initial_generation contract and the supplied synthetic 200-task corpus, the declared generator produced validator-clean candidates for every task; the deterministic validator’s validation_after.violation_count was zero across episodes. This empirical fact explains the degenerate null: with no initial failures there was nothing for a bounded repair loop to correct under the preregistered adapter policy. The experiment therefore supports the conditional claim: "given a generator that produces validator-clean shared candidates on this synthetic task bank, a bounded validator/repair wrapper produces no measurable paired improvement." It does not answer the counterfactual of whether a repair loop would help when independent generation produces unsafe candidates, when repair budgets are larger, or when the validator semantics differ.

Design trade-offs and operational implications: Shared_initial_generation improves causal attribution (any discordance must come from repair) but reduces the probability of observing baseline failures. Practitioners and researchers should treat shared vs independent generation as answering distinct operational questions: (a) shared_initial_generation isolates repair effectiveness conditional on specific candidate-correction capability; (b) independent generation evaluates end-to-end production risk reduction when generation is stochastic. The archived bundle supports direct, reproducible follow-ups to cross this axis: (A) permit independent condition generation (two independent model calls per task) to increase baseline failure probability and enable repair opportunities; (B) increase repair budget or enable iterative/tool-assisted repair; (C) enrich the harm-oracle with vendor-specific semantics.

Statistical interpretation and degenerate CI: The observed paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] is degenerate because the contingency table has zero discordant pairs. This reflects a deterministic outcome in the archived artifact set, not a failure of the bootstrap procedure. In practice this result denotes that across the archived shared-initial candidates and deterministic validator semantics there was no observed room for repair to operate under the preregistered contract.

Construct and external validity cautions: The primary outcome depends on validator expressiveness and task-bank difficulty. Our synthetic task corpus encodes workflow constraints (e.g., make-before-break patterns and allowed-touched-field sets) but remains a sandbox: the deterministic Batfish-style validator used here does not emulate every vendor-specific nuance or production telemetry source. The run used a single declared generator family (gpt-5-mini) and a single bounded repair budget (≤1 repair), so conclusions do not generalize across models or repair strategies. Additionally, shared_initial_generation reduces the probability that generation variance will expose repair utility; thus absence of observed benefit does not imply absence of benefit under independent-generation, model heterogeneity, or adversarial perturbations.

Reproducible follow-ups enabled by archived artifacts: The execution bundle contains every per-episode trace, the full validator rule-set, the task manifest, raw model responses, and reconciliation logs. This allows three direct reproducible experimental variants without additional code invention: (1) switch to independent generation by using separate model calls per condition while reusing the same task manifest; (2) increase the repair budget to allow iterative repair and record the added repair-related provider calls and repair_prompt traces; (3) swap or extend the Batfish-style harm-oracle with vendor-augmented rules captured in a provided validator-rule extension slot. All of these variants are supported by the archived artifacts and the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter configuration entries.
sections.conclusion: We executed a sealed preregistered paired trial to measure the marginal effect of a deterministic Batfish-style validator in a bounded generate→validate→repair pipeline under a shared_initial_generation contract. For the synthetic 200-task bank and declared generator (gpt-5-mini), every shared initial candidate passed the deterministic validator: both baseline and guarded arms were validator-clean on all tasks, giving an exact paired difference of 0.0 (95% CI [0.0,0.0]; McNemar p = 1.0). No repairs were invoked, so repair efficacy was not observed. These artifact-grounded results do not refute the potential value of verifier-assisted workflows; rather they demonstrate that preregistered contract choices (shared vs independent generation), task-bank challenge level, validator fidelity, and repair policy jointly determine whether verifier assistance yields an observable benefit. The archived execution bundle contains all artifacts necessary to reproduce the run and to design follow-ups that trade off generator variance and repair opportunity to quantify repair-mediated gains in realistic settings.

Pre-lock infrastructure development and rehearsals were explicitly excluded from the empirical evidence presented here.
limitations: Confirmatory scope limited to a synthetic public task corpus and a deterministic Batfish-style sandbox; results do not generalize to production devices, multi-vendor heterogeneity, or richer harm oracles.
Single declared model family tested (gpt-5-mini) and a single bounded repair budget (≤1 repair); no cross-model or multi-iteration repair claims are made.

The preregistered shared_initial_generation contract produced exactly one shared initial generation per task that was reused for both conditions; this reduces sensitivity to generator stochasticity and therefore reduced the likelihood of observing discordant pairs arising purely from generation variance.

The repair loop was never invoked because baseline produced zero validator-detected errors; therefore the preregistered secondary hypothesis about repair-success (>50%) could not be empirically evaluated.

Contamination and template-alignment risk: automated contamination checks recorded no flagged items, but pretraining memorization or template-alignment remains a construct-validity threat that automated checks cannot fully eliminate.
Adversarial and prompt-injection scenarios were not included; the study does not assess robustness under targeted attacks.
